title: Visiting Myrtle Beach in winter
summary: What stays open, what slows down and how to enjoy the quiet season
description: What to do in Myrtle Beach in winter: which attractions stay open, what closes for the season, and how to plan around fewer crowds and cooler weather.
intro: Winter on the Grand Strand is quiet. The beaches are empty, hotel rates drop and traffic eases. It is not beach weather, but it can be a good time to visit if you plan for it.

p: A number of seasonal attractions close or run reduced schedules. Water parks and some amusement rides close for the season, a few mini golf courses have shortened hours, and some small tours and outfitters stop running. Rooftop and patio bars are often closed or quiet. Always check an attraction's own page before you drive over.

list: Golf. Winter is the cheapest time of year, and many courses stay open.
Indoor attractions like WonderWorks, Ripley's Aquarium, the Pinball Museum and escape rooms.
Live shows and dinner shows, many of which run holiday productions in November and December.
Breweries, wine bars and the live-music venues that stay open year-round.
Nature: state parks, Brookgreen Gardens and the MarshWalk are good in cool, clear weather, and Brookgreen is known for a winter light display.
Georgetown's museums and Harborwalk, for a day trip.

p: Dolphins swim along the coast all year, so a cruise is possible if a company is running trips. Schedules thin out in winter, so call ahead and ask what the weather policy is.

Bring layers. Winter days can be mild one afternoon and cold the next, and the wind off the water makes it feel colder. Plan outdoor things for the middle of the day and keep an indoor backup for each day.
